title: 1995 AHSME Problem 29
statement: For how many three-element sets of positive integers \(\{a,b,c\}\) is it true that \(a\cdot b\cdot c=2310?\)

solutions.text: Since \(2310=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11,\) each prime belongs to exactly one of the three factors. If all factors exceed \(1,\) their unordered prime groups form a partition of five objects into three nonempty blocks, counted by \[ S(5,3)=\frac{3^5-3\cdot2^5+3}{6}=25. \] If one factor is \(1,\) the primes are partitioned into two nonempty blocks, giving \(S(5,2)=2^4-1=15.\) The factors are distinct because their disjoint prime sets differ. Thus the total is \(25+15=40,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: Factor \(2310\) into distinct primes and assign each prime to one of the factors
Count separately the cases in which one factor is \(1\) and in which all three factors exceed \(1\)
